name: Evidence Citation Profiling
description: Analyzes the structural patterns used to introduce and integrate evidence, citations, or examples. AI models exhibit a highly rigid, formulaic approach to citing sources, whereas human writers integrate evidence organically and unevenly.
algorithm: Syntactic Dependency Parsing & Citation Rhetoric Analysis
mechanism: When supporting an argument, human writers integrate evidence using highly varied, context-dependent structures. A human might drop a citation in parentheses at the absolute end of a paragraph, weave a quote messily into the middle of their own sentence, or reference an author informally ('As Smith argues...'). Large Language Models, optimized for RLHF (Reinforced Learning from Human Feedback) training to appear 'helpful and authoritative', default to rigid, templated evidentiary structures. They habitually use textbook-style introductory clauses ('According to a recent study by...', 'For example, research has shown that...'), followed immediately by a neatly summarized, standalone declarative sentence. They rarely employ parenthetical asides for core evidence or weave direct quotes seamlessly into complex compound sentences. This method uses dependency parsing to map the syntactic distance between evidentiary markers (e.g., 'according to', 'cited by', 'study shows') and the actual claimed facts. A text that introduces evidence exclusively through symmetrical, textbook-standard introductory clauses—lacking the fluid syntactic integration characteristic of human thought—is flagged as highly algorithmic.
useCase: Essential for auditing student essays, academic research papers, and argumentative articles where the 'mechanics of proof' distinctly reveal the author's origin.
strengths:
• Highly effective against 'academic' prompts; even when instructed to write an essay, AI cannot easily replicate the messy, organic way humans weave citations into their own cognitive flow.
• Explores the rhetorical structure rather than just vocabulary, making it resilient against simple synonym replacement (spinning).
• Captures the psychological aspect of RLHF training, where models are heavily penalized for unsupported claims, forcing them into predictable 'claim + textbook citation' loops.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives in rigid academic writing environments (like certain scientific abstracts or legal briefs) where strict, formulaic citation guidelines are enforced by standard formats.
• Completely blind in creative fiction or casual texts where empirical evidence and citations are naturally absent.
• Relies on identifying known evidentiary markers; highly atypical citation styles might completely bypass the syntactic parser.
parameters:
Analysis: Linguistic Dependency Parsing & Evidentiary Marker Extraction
Metric: Syntactic Rigidity of Evidence Integration vs Fluid Baseline
Output: 0-100 Citation Formulaic (Algorithmic Rigidity) Score
accuracy: High — 82-89% on argumentative and academic texts. It accurately targets the 'helpful but robotic' structural tics imposed by safety and alignment training.

references.title: Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
Jawahar, G. et al. (2020). Automatic Detection of Machine Generated Text: A Critical Survey. COLING.
